en: Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Venerable Pingshi of Tiantong.
In the seventeenth year of the Zhizheng era, the Dharma descendant of the eighteenth generation of the Linji lineage, Chan Master Pingshi Ding of Tiantong, [composed this].

He manifested his parinirvāṇa in the Eastern Hall after another nine years. His disciples, including Dayong and others, collected the teachings he had delivered during his three assemblies and carved them onto woodblocks for circulation.
As I was fortunate enough to have personally encountered this Chan Master, they requested me to write a preface. I humbly reflect that Linji was the tenth generation descendant of Bodhidharma;
through his great capacity and great function, he propagated the essential meaning of the "separate transmission outside the teachings. His saving of sentient beings was beyond measure.
The lineage reached its zenith as it was transmitted through successive generations to Master Wuzhun Fan of Mount Jing. His school flourished even further.
Wuzhun transmitted it to Master Xiyuan Hui of Tiantong, who in turn transmitted it to Master Dongyan Ri; both were those who attained the Way and were able to expand their lineage.
As the direct descendant of Xiyuan and the foremost disciple of Dongyan, his status and reputation were preeminent. Thus he [served] as...

The successor was Chan Master [Name]. Furthermore, he was able to cause his Way to flourish greatly in the southeast; among the scholars of the realm, there were none who did not revere him as their master.

When observing him during his formal expositions and debates, his methods of seizing and releasing, or taking and yielding, were like the rushing of thunder and the flashing of lightning—startling the spirit and dazzling the eyes, beyond all possibility of conjecture. Yet, he caused his students’ doubts to dissolve with clarity and transcend...
Nevertheless, it was because there was attainment. Had it not been for one who excelled in the functional application of Linji’s teachings, how could such a thing have been possible?

Is this not what is meant by "the root being firm, the branches flourish; the source being distant, the stream becomes ever clearer"? At the beginning of the Southern Song dynasty, the study of Chan was in great decline.
Students failed to recognize the functional application of Linji and often fell into the heterodox meditation of silent illumination. My ancestor Miaoxi exerted his efforts...
Only after this was it rectified, and thus Chan study became correct. The Master’s conduct was upright yet harmonious, and his speech was concise and essential.
In his leisure time, he devoted his writings primarily to refuting heterodox doctrines; was this not perhaps the intention of Miaoxi? Alas, the Master has passed away and can no longer be seen.
If one wishes to seek a semblance of his Way, what recourse is there but this record? From where else could one turn?
Suddenly, someone questioned me, saying, "Dharma did not establish written words; yet you, Meditation Master, have preserved this record.
Is this not a contradiction? I replied to him, "That Dharma did not establish [written words] was precisely to remove the obscuration of written words."

The Chan Master preserves that which is true; thus he clarifies the intent of the Separate Transmission. If one can indeed dispel their obscurations and grasp this intent, would that not be excellent?
Vimalakīrti said, "Rely on the meaning, not on the words," and further, "Words and written characters are all marks of liberation.
How profound! How profound! The questioner remained silent. Thereupon, [the author] wrote this as the "Chan of the Level Stone."
Preface to the Recorded Sayings of the Master. Written by the Śramaṇa Zhìrén of Póyáng, former abbot of Chóngbào Chan Monastery in Shàoxīng.
Table of Contents for the Recorded Sayings of Wànshí Wǎnghé.
Preface to the Discourse Record of Baosheng Chan Monastery and the Discourse Record of Dingshui Chan Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture.
Epilogue to the Verses and Eulogies for the True Portrait in the *Recorded Sayings* of Tiantong Chan Monastery;
and the *Recorded Sayings* of Master Pingshi upon his First Appointment at Baosheng Chan Monastery in the Prefecture of Qingyuan.
Compiled by the Dharma-heir Bhikṣus Wénxī and others of Zhēnrú Chán Monastery in Tāizhōu.
On the fifteenth day of the third month in the third year of the Dàdé era, the Master entered the monastery. Incensing the Buddha Hall, he said: "The Buddha-body is unconditioned;
it does not fall into any numerical categories. A dried piece of excrement. Three catties of hemp. *Nian*. He then prostrated himself.
The Patriarch’s Hall: vast and expansive, a hundred uglinesses and a thousand clumsinesses. A man from Fusang plowing a field in Shensi.
One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. Entering the room, he brandishes his staff.
Deshan’s blow, Linji’s shout—rocks split, cliffs crumble, thunder rolls, lightning flashes. He plants it down.
Master, the noble one may ascend eight steps.
Ascending the seat, he holds up the incense and says:

"This incense is respectfully offered to pray for the longevity of the present Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years. Next, holding up the incense, he says: "On behalf of..."
He went to see the Great Master Dayan at Dongyan of Tiantong Jingde Chan Monastery on Mount Taibai.
He burned incense in a single burner, not to repay kindness or gratitude, but simply to humiliate him. He then took his seat.

Monk Yanqing struck the gavel and said, "In this Dharma assembly of dragons and elephants, you should contemplate the primary principle. The Master said, "If it is the primary principle," [he would have to burn another burner].
Truly, there is no place to set down one's words. Is there anyone here now who would ask a question? I, this mountain monk, shall meet you at the gateway of the second meaning.
A monk stepped forward and said: "The realm and its phenomena pervade the universe; a surging aura of auspiciousness fills the forests and hills.
You wield the Diamond Sword that kills and gives life; its chilling divine radiance pierces the Dipper and Ox. [The Master] opened the hall for the sake of the nation.
“I wish to hear the essential meaning of the Dharma. The Master said, “Upon the summit of Mount Zhurong, dewdrops fall upon the ten-thousand-year-old pines.

The student asked, “If that is so, then the four seas are all brought under the sovereign’s transformation; this is the ‘Ten-Thousand-Year Joy’ song of our own house. The Master said, “He has spoken it from his very mouth.
The student asked, “As for Mazu Daoshi’s saying, ‘This very mind is Buddha; neither mind nor Buddha,’ what was his intended meaning?”

"What? the Master said. "The permanent residence lasts for a thousand years; the monk exists for a single morning. The student asked, "When the myriad functions have ceased and even the thousand sages carry nothing with them, what then?
The Master said, "It is pure when the eyes do not see. The student asked, "The moon in the empty expanse over the azure pool of ten thousand ages."
"Only after repeatedly pulling and searching can one begin to know. The Master said, "The chaotic assembly of Chan practitioners is like hemp and millet.
The monk bowed. The Master said, "As expected. He then continued: "Outside the gate, the lake light is deep and clear; atop the eaves, the green bamboo is lush. Carriages and horses jostle together;
human smoke and dwellings are dense and intermingled. Wisdom cannot know it; consciousness cannot perceive it. This is what is called 'Buddha to Buddha, hand to hand.'"

To bestow this matter, the patriarchs have transmitted it from one to another as the transmission of this school. [The Master] suddenly grasps his staff: Heaven revolves to the left, Earth turns to the right;
the sun rises in the east, the moon sets in the west. A single path of empty stillness, radiantly luminous—thus, one is separated from the great trichiliocosm;
not thus, one is within the range of the lips. Under the Great Yuan’s unified empire, the borders are vast; may we offer our vows of auspiciousness!
"May our Lord live for ten million years!
[Zhuo] raised his staff and further recited the verse of Master Bodhidharma: "I originally came to this land / To transmit the Dharma and save deluded beings.
/ One flower opens into five petals; / The fruit ripens naturally. The Master said, "To speak thus is much like acting as if there were no one else around," and struck him.
The whisk-bearer said: "This year the peach and plum blossoms are precious; each single fruit is worth a thousand pieces of gold.
He descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven—eagles' eyes and dragons' pupils cannot grasp them.
Seven, six, five, four, three, two, one—those with iron foreheads and copper heads cannot leap out. Blazing like a fierce flame, sharp as a hair-cutting blade; to approach it..."
If you try to strike it with a torch, you will face the gate directly; if you aim at it, you will wound the edge and injure your hand. Apart from these two paths, how can one proceed?
Suddenly, if someone were to come forth from among the assembly, overturn the meditation seat, and shout to disperse the multitude—even Baosheng could not blame him.
Thereupon, he descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Lu Zu faced the wall; Xuefeng rolled the ball. One string moved and another melody was heard; leaves fall and one knows autumn.
But what is it like when you understand it in this way? A bronze oil-sieve filled to the brim with oil."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Sharing a bed, yet each dreams differently; of different surnames, yet dwelling together. A thousand transformations, ten thousand changes—little is real, much is empty.
He now is not me, and I now am not he. Do not take a white-fanged tiger and call it a black cat."
Winter Solstice Small Sermon: Within the gate of the patch-robed monks, there is a plot of ground where neither sun nor shade exists.
It is level and upright, standing solitary and precarious. It is near, within the space of an inch; yet it is far, beyond the great trichiliocosm.
Though it has been blown by the winds and scorched by the sun many times, and though for many years it has been overgrown with weeds and moss, you all have never once cast your eyes upon it.
If you look and see it, the myriad phenomena are shimmering with light. If you look and do not see it, the myriad phenomena are shimmering with light.
What is it like when it is neither thus nor otherwise? A parched brick strikes one through to the very marrow; a single branch of red flame erupts from an icy river.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Outside the mind there are no dharmas; outside dharmas there is no mind. From where do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth come?
He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall again, he cited the case of Master Sanjiao. A monk asked, "What are the Three Jewels? He replied, "Rice, wheat, and beans."
The Master said: "When Sanjiao speaks in this way, it is much like taking the property of the Sangha and using it for one's own personal enjoyment;
alas, it is enough to provoke the laughter of bystanders. Suppose someone were to ask Baosheng, 'What are the Three Jewels? I would simply tell him: 'Buddha, Dharma, Sangha. Why?
Because a thousand falsehoods are not equal to a single truth."
A Small Sermon on New Year’s Eve: The first word and the final phrase cannot be borne by the great earth; they cannot be blocked by the Buddha’s hand.

To those of us who wear the patched robe, it is as if we do not see what is seen, and as if we do not hear what is heard. When walking, simply walk; when sitting, simply sit. When hungry, eat your rice.
In the cold, one turns toward the fire. What does it matter that the stars shift and the constellations change, that winter comes and summer goes?
Outside the gate, the northern wind blows piercingly—who among you is a traveler on the road? Before the eaves, the frozen sun shines warmly—all are guests who have reached home.
For tonight, I, Baosheng, cannot avoid roasting the white ox of the open field; I shall share the New Year with you all. Suddenly, he took up his staff and struck the ground.
One look. Next year there will be new branches again; the wind of spring vexes all, never ceasing. Again, he raised the case:
A monk asked an ancient worthy, "What is it like when the year is spent and the age is exhausted? The ancient worthy said, "Every house looks upon the wild fox cubs.
The verse says: "Every house looks upon the wild fox cubs; this is precisely when the year is spent and the age is exhausted. Why?
Like Liao Huzi of the Eastern Village, he holds his iron flute upside down and blows it against the wind.

On the occasion of the Lantern Festival, he ascends the hall and says: "In the school of the patch-robed monks, there is a special rule: where a path is found, the path is blocked; where a bridge is crossed, the bridge is severed."
One must know that on the fifteenth day of the first month, it is certainly the Lantern Festival. [The Master] throws down his whisk and says:
"I see that the lamp-light Buddha’s original radiance and auspicious signs are just like this."

On the anniversary of the Buddha’s Nirvana, he ascended the hall and said: "The World-Honored One, as he was about to enter Parinirvāṇa, rubbed his chest with his hand and addressed the assembly, saying:
'You should all carefully contemplate my purple-golden body; gaze upon it until you are fully satisfied. Do not let yourselves have cause for regret later.
Today it exists, but tomorrow it will be no more. Those who say that I have entered extinction are not my disciples; those who say that I have not entered extinction are likewise not my disciples.'"
"You are not my disciple. At that time, the assembly of a hundred trillion beings all attained realization. The verse says:
"I thought no one could recognize him, Yet at his departure he flaunted his body of purple-gold. At that moment, none in the assembly understood;
Only Pāpīyas was granted the title of a true man."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time speak dreams; the six ancestral patriarchs speak dreams; the old monks throughout the land speak dreams.
Is there anyone here who shares the same dream as those on their own beds? Come forward and speak! After a long silence, he said: 'When a person is poor, their wisdom is short.'"
The horse is lean and its hair is long.

A small *śamatha* (summer retreat) discourse: The *pariniṣpanna-kāya* (perfected monastery) of Perfect Enlightenment encompasses the entire dharma-realm; through the wisdom of equality, the form-body is universally manifested.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, one is always within it. Seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing—nothing surpasses this.
This karmic consciousness of sentient beings is the original source of all Buddhas; that which is the original source of all Buddhas is precisely the karmic consciousness of sentient beings.
Therefore it is said: "Those who are deluded regarding what the Buddhas have awakened to are called sentient beings;
those who have awakened to what sentient beings are deluded about are called Buddhas. Suddenly, someone might come forth from among the assembly and say:
"What place is this, speaking of delusion and awakening? I know you are making your living inside a ghost cave! After a long silence, [the Master] takes up his staff.
"For now, let us leave it leaning against the wall; the straw sandals shall dry in the sun, awaiting the autumn wind.

He ascended the hall and said: "Master Zhao [Zhu Fonian] said: 'That all phenomena are without difference—does this mean that one must first cut off the crane and lengthen the duck, or level the mountains and fill the valleys, before they can be called non-different?
The Master said: 'Master Zhao propagated the sutras and composed treatises; he may truly be called..."
He was proficient in both doctrine and practice. Yet, within the gate of the patch-robed monks, he has not even let them drink a drop of water. Baosheng dares to say:
if you wish for the myriad dharmas to be without distinction, you must directly cut off the crane to match the duck’s height and level the mountains to fill the valleys.
Nevertheless, those who laugh at me are many; those who smile with understanding are few.
Ascending the hall to open the furnace: The single transmission of Shaoshi has grown cold like ashes over the years. Today, for your sake, I shall open this furnace with both gentle and fierce fires.
(He strikes the whisk and descends from his seat.)
Dharma Ji’s offering of incense is a great calamity. He stubbornly claims he is the First Patriarch; a sweet melon is sweet from stem to tip, a bitter gourd is bitter from root to fruit.
This misfortune extends to his descendants, each of whom hammers a stake and rows a boat. A wooden man with no tongue laughs at the spring breeze;
a lantern swallows the pillar of exposed light.

On the eighth day of the fourth month, he proceeded to the invitation at Ding-shui and took his leave of the assembly by ascending the hall. "When the World-Honored One appeared in the world, Bao Sheng withdrew;
both were great men, each walking his own path. He raised his staff and struck it once. "The traces of his spiritual presence remain even where the monkeys cry."
The Recorded Sayings of Master Píngshí at Dìngshuǐ Chán Monastery, compiled by his disciples Zǐchǎng, Liǎoyīn, and others.
On the twelfth day of the fourth month in the second year of the Huángqìng era, the Master entered the monastery. Pointing to the mountain gate, he said: "A hundred thousand dharmas..."
The Gate. At every gate there is a path. A frog leaps up to the Brahma Heaven; an earthworm brushes past the Eastern Sea. Pointing to the seat:
"The one path leading upward is not transmitted by the thousand sages. Level as heaven, level as earth; the face of the sun, the face of the moon.
He then ascended the seat and offered incense, making his vow.
The Master retired to his seat. A monk came forward and said, “When the World-Honored One held up the flower and Kāśyapa smiled, what was the meaning of this?
The Master said, “Do not mistake the cry of a crane for the song of a warbler. The monk pressed further, “The World-Honored One said, ‘I have the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye;
I entrust it to Mahākāśyapa. What does this mean? The Master said, “One dog barks at the void; a thousand...”
Mao Jianshi stepped forward and said, "At Vulture Peak, the Flower was held up to entrust the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye.
Today, at Shuangfeng, as you open the hall for the assembly, what instruction do you ultimately have to bestow? The Master said, "The bright sun hangs in the sky; the clear breeze pervades the earth.
Jianshi said, "When there is spirit, add to that spirit; where there is no elegance, there too is elegance. The Master said, "Be careful not to thrust your needles and awls about in confusion."
The monks prostrated. The Master then said: "The great capacity responds universally; the great function manifests before us. A single phrase settles the ancestral school;
the body lies across the universe. Have you not seen? When Baoshou opened the hall, Sansheng pushed forward a monk, and Baoshou struck him immediately—cutting through nails and severing iron.
Sansheng said, 'To act for others in this way not only blinds this monk's eyes, it blinds yours as well.'"
This has taken away the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou! The sword that kills; Baoshou hurls down his staff and returns directly to the abbot’s quarters.
The blade that gives life. Excellent, great assembly! It is like a general who carries these seven items with him and is seasoned in the fray of battle.

It is not merely a matter of swift as lightning or galloping like a star; it is truly to transcend the present and surpass the past. Just as when this mountain monk opens the hall today, what exactly does he clarify?
After a long silence: "On the three borders there is no need for weapons; ten thousand miles sing songs of celebration for Great Peace."

On the occasion of the opening of the summer retreat, the Master ascended the hall and raised the precedent of Dongshan Wushan, who addressed the assembly, saying: "For this summer retreat, I have no offerings to present to the great assembly.
I shall instead host a private banquet to attend to you all. He then raised his hand and said: "Luo-luo, summoning; Luo-luo, beckoning;
Luo-luo, seeing you off. Do not resent my lack of formality. I humbly pray that you will all take care. The Master remarked: "Dongshan Wushan’s arrangement was indeed such as this."

Such formalities, when carried to excess, become flattery; the water of meditative concentration (*samādhi*) is not thus. [The Master] suddenly grasps his staff, steps down from the left side, and ascends the hall.
An ancient said: "I have a phrase; I shall wait until a horned ox gives birth to a child before I speak it to you.
Now tell me, what is this one phrase? Double Peak, without sparing a single hair on his brow, shall explain it through for all of you. If...
"To call this 'a single phrase' is like being shot into hell by an arrow. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The various kinds of spiritual sprouts grow in spring and flourish in summer; wherever the hand reaches to pluck them, there is nothing that is not medicine.
Suddenly picking up his staff, he called to the assembly, saying: "This is the staff. Can you call it medicine? He then threw it down.
The Master said: "If there is a sinew in your eyes, you must discern this: Mañjuśrī was once deceived by Sudhana. Ascending the hall, he said:
"On the fifteenth day of the fourth month, it is bound; twisting leftward, they twist straw ropes to bind the ghost-child.

On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, it is released; holding chopsticks upside down, they stir the vast ocean. For the patch-robed monks, do not admire the various sages, and do not prize your own spiritual brilliance. To be liberated..."
Briefly discarding the customs of antiquity and shattering the molds of the present age, he raises his staff:
he has not yet had leisure to offer a bundle of fresh fodder, yet the six-ringed golden bells resound through the distant void.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "There is one person who always remains at home, never leaving the road; there is another person who always remains on the road, never leaving home.
Taking up his staff, he said: 'The nostrils of both these fellows have been pierced through by Shuangfeng.'"
The Master of the Hall: "Without experiencing a single matter, one does not grow a single bit of wisdom.

Entering the hall: "More than half a month of early summer has passed; heat spreads across the heavens and the earth. As for the patch-robed monks, their noses are straight and their eyes are askance."
That fellow has no blood beneath his skin. During the ninety-day retreat of the summer rains, he merely claims to pity the swan and protect the snow;

yet he further speaks of attaining realization within a fixed period—this is much like nailing a stake into empty space. Boiling sand will not necessarily produce rice; how can a mirage quench thirst?
On the Twin Peaks there is nothing to be measured or discussed. I offer you this one phrase directly: simply be able to leave the mind free from affairs.
Spontaneously responding to the time and the season, he struck the whisk and descended from his seat.
Entering the hall: "The rain of the sixth month is priceless treasure; the high fields and low fields are brimming with water. Early and late rice crops are shrouded in misty clouds;
farmers gather their heads to speak of a bountiful year. Three coins for a peck of rice can surely be guaranteed. For the patch-robed monks, there is nothing—*no-mu*.
The head and brain. Eating one’s fill and sleeping. Few know how to be grateful.
A small *cankuan* (sermon) upon the conclusion of the summer retreat: Grasping and releasing the mouth of the *pudao* (cloth bag); swallowing up mountains, rivers, and the great earth.
The monk’s staff comes horizontally and goes vertically; it carries the sun, moon, and stars upon its pole. Suchness in principle and suchness in phenomena; fully master and fully guest. How elegant!
Truly elegant! Extraordinary, indeed extraordinary! [The Master] strikes the meditation seat. "When the path to the water's end is exhausted, sit and watch the clouds arise.

Again, he cites: "In the scriptures it is said that those who recite the Vinaya eighty times for the duration of a summer retreat may not attain the four fruits of sainthood, yet they will surely realize the third [fruit]."
The Master said, "To practice by clinging to the fundamental text is like a donkey pulling a millstone. How should a monk of our school act? After a long silence, he said:
'Having a mouth, it is only fit to hang idly on the wall.'"
Ascending the hall, he held up his rosary and said: "A hundred and eight mani beads strung on a single thread;
this year counts on until next year, and next year begins again from the start—a hundred and eight mani beads strung on a single thread. Tell me, assembly:
if it does not stop at five before, nor reach seven after, what is it ultimately? The Great Statue of Jiazhou eats too much salt. Shaanfu...
The iron ox grows ever thirstier. Entering the hall for discourse:
Movement is like drifting clouds; stillness is like the valley spirit. Do not mistake the Big Dipper for the Southern Star.
Just as this mountain monk has been for the past month—half-emerging, half-entering; sometimes to the east, sometimes to the west—what, in the end, has he accomplished?
Matters of the Frontier: Turning my head, the red dust has buried the horses deep; the traveler lies even further beyond the green mountains.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case: Yunmen held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying, "The staff has transformed into a dragon and swallowed up heaven and earth.
From where do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth come? Master Dongyan, my late teacher, commented: "Heaven..."
The staff also has its master. Although it does not undergo transformation, it is simply easy to see yet difficult to recognize.

[The Master] throws down the staff and says: "I told you it was a dragon, yet you stubbornly did not believe; wait until it brings down the rain before you shall know. The Master takes up the staff and summons the assembly, saying:
"When an object meets its master, the eye stands firm. He plants the staff upright and says: "One only knows that opening one's mouth is easy; one does not realize..."
[The Master] with a long tongue ascends the hall.
A poem by the Chan master Hanshan says: "A white crane carries bitter flowers, flying a thousand miles in a single breath;
wishing to go to Mount Penglai, it takes these as its provisions. O virtuous Chan practitioners, many have had a sudden flash of insight here, yet they have misunderstood.
Those who do so are not few. Thus it is said: "My poetry is indeed poetry; some call it verse (gāthā). Poetry and verse are essentially the same;
when reading them, one must be careful."
Ascending the hall on the ninth day: Today is the ninth day of the ninth month; calling out to one another, no hand is extended.

If you are one who dwells within this circle, a single thought will suffice to know it exists. Striking the meditation seat, he said: "The golden rooster flies up onto the jade balustrade; with one cry, it shatters the dawn across a thousand peaks."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: Once while Mazu was gazing at the moon, Zhiang, Baizhang, and Nanquan were standing in attendance. Mazu asked, "At this very moment, what is it? Zhiang said, "This is precisely the time for cultivation.

Baizhang said, "This is precisely the time for making offerings. Nanquan, however, shook his sleeves and departed. Mazu remarked, "The Sutras return to the Tripitaka; Zen returns to the sea. Only Puyan alone transcends the mundane world. The Master said: [The Master] said: "When the moon is full, there is no moon; when the moon is new, the moon is complete. When the wind blows, the trees bend; when the water flows, the waves rise.

At that very moment, how can one speak? If you say 'cultivation,' you are still caught in the net of practice. If you say 'offerings,' you are still bound by the traces of dharma. To shake the sleeves and depart—this is the true freedom. Yet even so, it is like a blind man looking at the sky: though he sees nothing, the sky is not hidden. Do you understand? If you do not understand, go and look at the moon yourself."
The Master of Ma and his entire family, father and son, only know how to greedily gaze at the moon in the sky; they do not realize they have lost the oar in their own hands.
Shuangfeng was not like this. At such a time as this, what then? Even the blue sky must receive a blow of the staff.

Returning from the Hall after viewing the scriptures at the Universal Dharma-Assembly, [the Master] ascends the platform and says: "The entire Great Canon of the Teachings is a 'cutting word' (a homophone).
But tell me, what word does it cut? You worthy ones, having left one forest monastery and entered another community, you have spent seven days reading them morning and night.
Is there anyone among you who has seen through them completely? If you have seen through them, not only will you be able to look up to and repay..."
"Saintly grace! This is indeed a source of personal joy and relief. Had you not seen through this, your eyes would have been replaced by black beans.
Suddenly he brandishes his staff; "Shuangfeng spares no effort with his eyebrows, employing skillful means to meet everyone at the gateway of the second meaning.
He plants the staff firmly on the ground: "He drives out Kauśika from the bustling marketplace and startles the doltish ones awake."
The Brahma King sleeps. [The Master] ascends the hall and says: "Monks of the patched-robed community only know how to climb higher step by step; they do not know how to let go from the void.
Tell me, where does the error lie? After a long silence, he says: "Descend from the seat and circulate through the hall for tea."
Ascending the hall, [Baizhang] held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying: "If you have a staff, I give you a staff;
if you have no staff, I take away your staff. Later, Master Zhenjing commented on this, saying:
"If you have a staff, I take away your staff; if you have no staff, I give you a staff."

"Master Zhang. The Master said, "These two great elders conduct their business within the realms of existence and non-existence, or gain and loss. If one were to examine them closely, they both deserve a blow from the master’s staff.
However, Shuangfeng, unwilling to exhaust the Dharma to the point of having no subjects, lets them off by one stroke. He leaned on the staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Yunmen has a single song: 'The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. If you can understand it directly and immediately, I dare not yet grant you my approval.
Why? Because if one does not truly hit the tiger, one's efforts are in vain and the feathers are wasted."
The Small Sermon on the Eve of the Year’s End: The past has already passed; a cast-iron scale weight has been eaten through by worms.
The future is yet to come; a lantern climbs the wall up to the terrace. As for this very moment—the thirtieth day of the twelfth month—how is it with that which is presently here?
If there were even a single dharma, Vairocana would fall among the common folk. If there were not even a myriad dharmas, Samantabhadra would lose his way.

The Realm. (He raises the whisk. Pūrvavideha in the east, Aparagoyānī in the west, Jambudvīpa in the south, and Uttarakuru in the north—right now, they are all turning the Great Dharma Wheel upon the tip of this mountain monk’s whisk. Do you people see them yet?

Ascending the hall, he said: "The gradual heat of early summer is an annual occurrence; the Tathāgatas of the three periods do not know it at all.

Small-scale *Xichan* (Summer Retreat) *Shanchan* (General Preaching). The teachings have flowed into this age of semblance; the Sage is distant in time. The land is vast and people are sparse; words are many, yet the Way is far.

when the true command is put into practice, the ten directions are cut off at their seat. Thus, from the assembly on Vulture Peak to the summit of Shaoshi Mountain, he brings it forth with his bare hands.
Lying across the body to bear the burden: at Deshan’s staff, he deceives the Hu and hoodwinks the Han; under Linji’s shout, there is little substance and much emptiness.

Splitting Mount Taihua and diverting the Yellow River, it truly causes the stars to shift and the constellations to change. Striking the golden rooster and brushing the jade hare, it naturally becomes transparent and unobstructed from all eight directions.
This is the day when horses are returned and oxen rested; it is the time of woodsmen’s songs and fishermen’s chants. Maheshvara...
The True Eye is penetratingly clear; the numinous talisman behind the elbow radiates its brilliance. At such a time as this, how is it? The heavens are high and the myriad forms are upright;
the seas are vast and the hundred rivers flow toward them.
Small Assembly. The matter of the ancestors from the very beginning lies only in the present moment. To lift it up, heaven turns and earth revolves; to let it go, a drop of water freezes into ice.
It is not found after a phrase or before a sound; naturally, it is revealed at every turn. The nine peaks stand tall in their verdant green.
The twin ponds ripple with clarity; this is the place where Hongzhi revived the tradition. Truly, it was the site where his ancestors first proclaimed the Way.

To continue their noble legacy, I feel a sense of shame upon my breast. Thus, conditions arise from forms, yet forms themselves are not real. When both conditions and forms are forgotten, [one attains liberation].
Every step encountered obstruction. He raised his staff; when the staff was held horizontally, the mountains, rivers, and the great earth were all horizontal at once.

the lanterns remained as lanterns; the pillar remained as a pillar. Although it is thus, consider this: as for Yunmen—

The monk said, "If you answer questions like this, Master, you will have to buy more straw sandals to travel before you are finished. Qi called the monk forward.

only the blue-eyed barbarian monk smiles and nods his head."
Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "What is the Way? Nanquan replied, "The ordinary mind is the Way.
"Great assembly, amidst suffering and joy, adversity and favor, where the grease and fire burn one another, ten thousand births and deaths occur in a single kṣaṇa.
How can you attain the state of ordinariness? To reach this point, you must first attain clarity."
Nirvana Hall Sermon: The Eye-Treasury of the True Dharma, the wondrous mind of Nirvana— In the East, dry calabashes; in the West, rotten vines.
Wildfire burns them every year, yet they spring up anew when the spring breeze blows upon them.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: Zen Master Tiānyī Huái addressed the assembly, saying: "The green creeper winds its way up to the very top of the cold pine;
the white clouds float lightly, appearing and disappearing within the great void. The clouds rise on the southern mountain, and the rain falls on the northern mountain.
Do you understand? A sweet melon is sweet all the way to the stem; a bitter gourd is bitter down to the root. Master Yìng’ān commented: "Tiantóng does so as well."
The next move: the green creeper winds its way straight up to the summit of the cold pine; the white clouds, limpid and vast, appear and vanish within the great void.
A dog’s tail writes Sanskrit characters; a wild fox’s den is the palace of the Brahma King. The Master said:
"I, this mountain monk, when there is a staff, I raise it; when there is no staff, I follow precedent. Today, too, I make a move: the green creeper winds its way straight up..."
Ascending to the summit of the cold pines, the white clouds are limpid and ethereal, appearing and disappearing within the vast void.

Ascending the hall for the commencement of the summer retreat: One year is one year; one month is one month; one day is one day;
one moment is one moment. The sacred regulation lasts for ninety days; each of you must exert yourselves. Within this interval, there is yet another matter that I cannot tell to you people.
After a long silence, he said: "Above all, do not seek the juice within a sesame cake."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Librarian does not recognize characters; the Attendant has attained Zen; the Head Seat has his own strengths—each sees but one side.
They overturn Dongshan’s Five Ranks and split open Linji’s Three Mysteries. Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, the waves surge to the heavens."
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "The Buddha-dharma pervades the world, yet the mouth that speaks of the profound remains closed.
Hand in hand with the Wooden Seat Patriarch, we chant atop the high terrace. Now tell me: when Mount Taibai and Linglong Rock compete for the forehead, what exactly is being measured?
(He strikes the ground with the staff. In the city of Hunan, the people are well-nourished; rice is cheap and firewood abundant, sufficient for all our neighbors."
Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth: "The fifth day of the fifth month; the Festival of Midsummer. The wondrous elixir of the immortals is right here at the tips of the hundred grasses.
If you casually catch its scent, your skull will split apart! [He lets out a shout. He descends from his seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Do you all understand? This morning marks the fifteenth day of the sixth month once again.
Cold and heat press one another; birth and death draw ever closer. As for this foul-smelling monk’s robe upon your bodies, have you yet managed to cast it off?
Whether you can cast it off or not, let that be for now. Tell me: when clouds rise on the southern mountain and rain falls on the northern mountain, what does it ultimately mean?"
"How can one say they understand? [The Master] gave a shout.

Offering incense on the anniversary of Dongyan Wushang’s passing: Xiangyan weeping for Master Muzhou with his staff; the poor man longing for old debts;

When one examines his robes and single garment, there is not a single thing; yet when one observes his outward demeanor, there are a thousand manifestations. He swings on a swing within the eyes of a gnat; he performs somersaults upon the back of empty space.
In his haste to take his leave, he is truly reckless; seeking the Dharma to benefit living beings, he seeks out his original friend. Be careful! Be careful!
Master Baozhi of Liang Garden has long since cast aside his status as an elder within the hall.
The monk Yuan of Jiangxi returns to Mount Lu;
the clouds atop the peaks of Mount Heng and the waters within Poyang Lake—both cloud and water are without mind. Though separated by a thousand li, our longing for one another remains.
The master is seven feet tall; he has six pairs of straw sandals. Go, go, and act with propriety; all these are your own.
Sent to Master Miaoyuan of Nanhu, a great master of the Tiantai and Huayan schools for generations.
A carriage spans across the azure jade, reflecting the golden sands. My son, do not be too late.
Let it be so. As for noble lineages such as the Cuis and Lus, there is no need for pride. The lotus pond reflects layers of still water; upon the lion throne, fresh flowers rain down day after day.
Cease your longing for the fragrant herbs of the Snowy Mountains; a multitude of children fill the gate, awaiting the gift of your chariot.
Seeing off Chan Master Yun on his way home to visit Master Yuansou of Mount Jing:
This old fellow at the mountainhead has reached eighty-one. In such a great Dharma-city of the Southeast, his twin hair-tufts have turned white with the passing years.

A single word can cause the ancient style to become pure once more. To benefit others, he does not employ the "striking the tiger" technique; in raising his son, how could he forget licking his wounds?
The Calf’s Sentiment: Sitting before the Bright Moon Hall through the deep night, a lingering ray of light reaches as far as the long-stalked star.
Presented to Layman Yang Jinxiu of Zhaotang:
Vast and boundless, you seek only outwardly; yet your own numinous light is inherently sublime. With direct realization, all phenomena are non-existent.
Phenomena: From the beginning, not a single thread has ever been hung upon them. Do not allow white jade to suffer even a slight blemish; let even bright pearls mingle with the turbid current.
Speak these words to the Recluse Yang of Zhaotang: Why must immortals still seek to be enfeoffed as marquises?
Presented to Attendant Jing of Xuefeng:
A precious mirror before the window remains forever open. Its profound, cold radiance penetrates the night altar. The myriad phenomena of the universe return to this single illumination;
Throughout the ten directions, not a speck of dust remains. Even if Nanyue were to polish it to perfection, How could it compare to that struck by Dongping?
It is broken! Look with a smile at the water-chestnut flowers blooming on the pestle’s tip. The spring breeze has vainly killed the old yellow plum.
To build a new monks’ hall, everyone should look:
what a fine monks’ hall it is! A single pillar still supports a single beam. Taibai is a famous mountain under heaven.
Victory! In the ancient Buddha-dharma of Xízhōu, the King reigns supreme. Beneath the three rafters, heaven and earth are vast; before the seven-foot mat, sun and moon endure long.
Whether sitting, reclining, walking, or thus abiding, his body spontaneously emits white light from between his brows.
In the following month, I composed verses in the style of Master Jiang to see off Attendant He-shan Ju:
Before Mount Mao within the mountains of He-shan, A single phrase for the occasion is not easily proclaimed. A spiritual bird nurturing its wings should choose its tree;
A fine horse that chases the wind requires no whip. The flowers bloom at Shaoshi and the man returns to his kingdom; The moon is full at Huating and the guest departs.
Boarding the boat, I feel boundless emotion meeting you as I grow old. As we gaze upon one another, our conversation reaches back to the Putong era.
Master Ying returns to his home in the Seven Min Mountains;
the scenery south of heaven is exquisite. Desiring to go but finding no means, my old age remains unbearably bitter. I envy you, who are truly like fresh milk.

Calf, sigh! I have already become a silkworm about to sleep. You must deeply reflect upon the beauty and ugliness of your surroundings; you must thoroughly master the thick and thin flavors of the world.
Cherish yourself, O guest at the gate of the Patriarchal Master: the Azure Dragon does not permit one to lie idle in a clear pool.

Seeing off the Venerable Yewang Xie, the Vinaya Master, as he pays homage to the Patriarchs—truly, one must believe there is another heaven within the alchemical flask. His conduct and concealment reach back to the presence of the Ancient Sovereign. A single brazier of yam fire outweighs five tripods of state;
the pine wind filling the hall is worth ten thousand pieces of gold. One should not begrudge a worn-out mat for the meditation couch; do not spare the effort to sweep the Patriarch’s temple grounds.
Falling bricks. When Mount Mao sent his son, was it not intentional? How could the bending of the arm ever turn outward?
In the same rhyme, I present this to Master Li of Upper Zhushan, while also addressing Master Lingshi Chan, with the single character "Xin" (Faith) as the root of the Way.
To see in form and seek in sound is truly difficult; such is the case at the gateway of the six faculties.
Abiding on the path of non-arising, what contemplation is there to be made? The wind and moon of the Zen grove are fully revealed; the waves and billows of the ocean of teachings are all overturned.
I send word to ask if the old Chan master is well: the spring waters of Jiahe are green before his window.
Next, following the rhyme of Master Wuyan, I send this verse to Jing, the Venerable Karmadāna:
Ten strikes of the mallet have made his tongue go bald; At the top of a hundred-foot pole, he turns his body. Dispersing his house and breaking up his family—this is surely for such a son;
Who else would sit waiting by the stump or climb the tree? The pine branches are frozen through by the snow before the crags; The peach blossoms float with fragrance from the cave.
Spring within. It would be well to cast off one's bones once more at the Dragon Gate; who says that only the unicorn with its single horn possesses auspicious signs?
Using the rhyme of my predecessor, I bid farewell to the Venerable Zheng:
This matter is fundamentally without deficiency; yet where the mind seeks application, it can never be fully encompassed. Amidst the clamor of black and white, there is but empty fame.
Appearance: Often vermilion and yellow, they are cross-referenced and collated. Parting the weeds and gazing at the wind, do not act with undue pretension;
playing the game as the occasion arises, simply follow the current. If we meet again on another peak in the future, I shall join you once more in resolving this old koan.
In Lamentation for the Abbot Chu-zang (Disciple of Master Wuji of Chunyu-an):
The ancients held that thirty years constitute a generation; to perish before one’s time is a matter for which there is no settled meaning.

Truly, those with form follow the transformation of things, yet it is possible to reach the realm of non-thought—a talent difficult to attain. Amidst the shadow of the long star, his words still linger; within the sound of spring rain, his dream persists.
It is not yet cold. Turning my head back, I behold the layered oceans of the Flower Treasury (Kusumatalagarbha). Where could I possibly find a place to lodge my grief?

Guest Master Long knows that when the Patriarch struck his tent-pole, there was neither ground nor spike. Standing alone and majestic, this is indeed beyond doubt; both host and guest are fully present.

As for "I," who else could it be that enters into Māra and enters into the Buddha? Before the stimulus, one can both release and seize; beneath the phrase, there is not even a hair’s breadth nor a speck of dust.
The fallen blossoms cover the ground as spring has already grown old; how many people know the secret intent of the Patriarchs?
Seeing off Vinaya Master Yun as he departs to attend upon Master Zhu Yuan of Zitaotou:
In this hall of mine, no larger than a pint, with whom can I join hands to discuss the gate of our school? At Caoxi there is a path, yet no one arrives;
at Shaoshi there is no person, yet the path remains open. What leisure have I for idle contemplation? I shall only leave my aged eyes to see you off.
Returning Geese. On this journey, do not be surprised that I have little to entrust you with. I am but an old man at the end of his days by the Eastern Sea.
Following the rhyme of Master Beiyin, I send off Attendant Hui back to Chaoyang:
The springtime of Shaoshi passes before my eyes; Standing alone in the wind, my thoughts linger on it with longing. Mist over the river, willows by the bank—a thousand strands of silk.
A cubit of mountain flowers and stream water form a single scroll of brocade. Do not seek gain or loss within the realm of the visible; rather, penetrate the profound mystery beneath words.
The old path to Chaoyang is as vast as the heavens, yet today why should it not be possible to wave one’s hand and return home?
Presented to the portrait of Li Yuequan:
Floating dust in the void, specks of grime in the mirror; In the space of a single snap of the fingers, a hundred-year life.

To fully realize that the fundamental substance is originally formless— Vainly do you speak of a distinct spirit at the tip of a hair. With crane-like hair and chicken-like skin, who am I? As for those with tiger-heads and swallow-chins...
Who is this? There is no use in vainly depicting those who have met face-to-face; the bright moon and autumnal spring water are naturally authentic.
No one is skilled at poking their head out from the treasury of the hidden; retreat and your footing will be secure. Even the Buddha-eye cannot perceive them, yet ordinary minds see them intimately.
Within the thousand worlds of the universe, there is but a single mote of dust beyond all measure. How laughable that the old man of Vaiśālī once again opened the Gate of Non-duality!
After Grand Master Mukan returned to Longxiang, his later disciples were truly formidable;
they diligently sought through study and practice. The Buddha-Dharma has its own north and south, yet the rivers and mountains know neither ancient nor modern.
The marsh grasses pity the misty leopard; the court birds cherish their nurtured plumage. Departing, I turn my head again and again; the hundred cities are shrouded in deep mist and water.
Inscribed on the Path Traversed by the Monk of the Chángchūn Pavilion, Zhùnzàng:
The secret chamber does not admit a breath of wind; After the cold ashes of a hundred thoughts have subsided, One’s own body dwells within a realm of harmonious qi.
Other lives have no limit; the joy of this path is inexhaustible. Sitting all day with a mind immersed in darkness, jar-flowers scatter red upon the table.

Master Mu has traveled to all quarters, and his understanding of the Buddha-dharma pervades the world. He speaks of the profound mystery without opening his mouth; ten thousand functions are all stilled and cut away, and not a single thing is brought forth.
"This place is Maitreya; there is no Sudhana and no gate. Tortoise hair and rabbit horns are transplanted into the eyes.
Master Jiangshan Sheng, the Vinaya Master, has returned victorious from the Dharma-battlefield of Jiangxi.
A phoenix chick flies out from the eagle’s nest; ascending the hall, the drum is beaten for a general invitation.
Look! It makes the horse-sieve of Jiangxi laugh to tears.
Presented to Attendant Ren of Donglin (a Japanese man):
The Tiger Creek is cut off at the Yanmen Pass; a single phrase is difficult to utter when the moment arrives. At midnight, the sun rises over the Fusang tree.
It emerges; the golden rooster flies up onto the jade balustrade.
Sent to Master Lingshi:
The South Mountain tiger has no teeth or gums; the stench of its breath blowing in one's face is unbearable to hear. Shooting at the rock, it was but an empty sound, vanishing in vain.
Feathers. One should simply be put to shame by General Li.
Master Jian pays homage at Potalaka;
in whose house is there no Avalokiteśvara? Why labor so diligently to seek it elsewhere? One must travel far across the ocean mountains for a single step.
It turns. The falling flowers and fragrant grasses signal that spring is deep.

To the practitioner Zhan from Quannan, I show that "serene stillness, unmoving" is true permanence. Within the gate of Shaoshi, this has not yet reached its full potential; were the entire earth gathered up, it would be like a grain of millet.
A single grain. The wooden ball has no mouth; it laughs at Master Zeng.
Sending off Venerable Xi to visit Master Ling Shi of Jingci:

the Southern Mountains rise in ten-thousand-fold layers like brocade cloud-screens. The Hall of the Mirror of the School is high and not easy to ascend; a hot shout and a wrathful fist must be clearly perceived.
I look back; from of old, Master Lao has never possessed local attachments.
For Xue Dou, Preceptor Heng, not a single trace of a character remains in his breast; the entire Tripitaka is but dust in his eyes. Spring returns to Jinjing, and the flowers are as [vivid as]—
O Sea, do not slander the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata.
Then, without oars or rudders, and without unfurling sails, the whale-waves of ten thousand *li* will be traversed in a mere glance, and you shall be laden with three hundred *li* pearls.
A *hu* measure. At the outset, one need not fear waves as high as mountains.
To Attendant Jun:
Do not resent that Tiantong’s mouth is narrow; from the beginning, there has been no dharma to deliberate upon. The rhinoceros fan is broken.
Thus it is. "He has won a full wind of purity throughout the Great Tang.
Master Yuan went to Jiangxi to pay homage to the Patriarchs;
he could not bear the "Winnowing Basket" of Jiangxi, who sells flour along with the chaff to seek advantage. He merely inherited empty echoes for eighty years.
4. Here, from the very beginning, I shall seize and defeat him.
It is said that all dharmas emerge from this sutra;
yet if one asks from where this sutra emerges, it is apart from any commentary or explanation of this sutra.
Yes. At that time, the layman Bi Fangling was wealthy;
why did you, Venerable One, return to Longhua to visit your teacher?
What kind of demonic influence taught you to wander as a pilgrim? What kind of demonic influence taught you to leave the household life? I am old and cannot pursue this inquiry further.
"You, go back to Fannian and ask Longhua.
Show it to the Elder of Pan;
Ruiyan repeatedly calls out, 'The Master! When karmic consciousness is vast and boundless, one has not yet attained emptiness. Today, Tiantong points this out once again."
He emerges. Furthermore, he exposes his family’s disgrace to others.
Having become a pure practitioner (*śrāmaṇera*), he wanders the lands;
there is no Bodhi tree, and the mirror is not a stand. To plant rabbit horns and tortoise hair within one's eyes—dragging along this stinking hide born of a mother.
A bag. Wandering South Peak in the morning, Tiantai in the evening.
Hearing the bell, its sound rings out clearly, announcing dawn and dusk. Reaching down to the deep springs and up to the clouds. Stop the faculty of hearing and you must listen.
Grasping. In this weary life, who can again turn back to hear hearing?

Jingsha Zhangsheng sought the Buddha’s illness, the Patriarch’s illness, and the illnesses of all sentient beings. How is it that patch-robed monks have so many ailments? If you recognize the root of the illness, there is no arising.
The place: "When the 'Blowing-Off-the-Hair' sword has been used, it must be sharpened immediately.
[This refers to] sending the Venerable Ruan, the Vinaya Master of Changlu, to enter Min Province to pay homage to the Patriarchs.

When the Dharma-battle on Mount Huai was unexpectedly lost, he took his staff and wooden sounding-block with him into the miasmic regions. At the tip of every blade of grass, he lightly brushes away [delusions].
Stop saying that the Buddha-dharma resides only in the South.
The Way-realizer of Tiantai is universally perfect;
who says he lacks the capacity for skillful means? He is accustomed to letting loose his "soft and stubborn" ways before others, his pair of eyes dark and piercing.
The Vinaya: Tiantai thoroughly investigated and transcended Old Hanshan;
the Venerable Nan paid homage at Putuo and traveled through Tiantai.
Northern and Southern schools each established their own sects, falling into the realm of right and wrong; he has now severed the stone bridge and the path of the mind.
Severed! Where is there that the feet and head are not perfectly pervasive?
Lamenting the "Tiger-Trapping" device of Master Wuyi before the Thousand-Fathom Cliff—when he brought it forth directly in the light, who could have known? The skull is dried up; where are the eyes?
Alive! This is precisely when empty space falls to the ground.
To Zen Master Cheng, who was staying overnight at Danxia during a cold spell: "The wooden Buddha was burned, filling the room with smoke; the master’s eyebrows and beard fell away entirely."
All is exhausted. In most quarters, this has been wrongly transmitted.
Attendant Shou returned to Min;

his service of attending to the master’s handkerchief and flask has fulfilled his vow. Gazing south toward the wind, he composes a verse on his retirement: "Xuansha did not go out; the flying kites [have returned]."
Ling: He broke the toes of his mother-born feet.
Following the rhyme of Master Yuejiang, I send this off for the Venerable Xian as he travels to Potalaka, Tiantai, the Stone Bridge, the southern side of the sea gate at Nanpan, and the east.
The Great Being and the Śrāvakas are not easily encountered; we shall meet before even stepping onto the boat’s railing.
It is finished. A vast net of a hundred thousand layers.
I present this to the master of arts, Chen Jingyou:
My lifespan is equal to that of empty space; empty space is likewise of the same age as I. Master, you may calculate the measure of empty space.
"Certainty. I and empty space shall pay the life-debt.

He said to his attendant, "Return to Tiantong in Min to deliver this one sentence for my son: 'In a house infected by poison, do not taste the water. Immediately, the chestnut bursts open, and heaven and earth are revealed."
The Eye. Tan Yuan had no mouth to curse Nanyang.
The Treasure Keeper pays homage to the Patriarch;

he travels to various quarters, for Tianran is a singular treasure hidden within the mountains. He does not exist within heaven, earth, or the universe. Before the cooking cloth is even spread, it is as if the structure is already complete.
Attained. The Old Barbarian wears golden rings on both ears.
Ning the Attendant examined the Master in Min;
he spat out the five flavors of Chan from all quarters. Gela, you are in charge of the rice fields for the rest of your life. Upon arriving home, there is no need to present the "perfect circle."
The signs are clear; the profound intent is manifest right before you.

Master Song has returned to the south of the spring, where the Buddha-land is revealed in its vast majesty. Through the ages, his spiritual traces have shone with brilliance. That he went nine times and ascended three times was merely a waste of effort for the arrogant.
Power! It does not hinder you from returning home to ask Master Zeng.
To the venerable Shibiao:
Amidst the cry of the cuckoo, the moon of the third watch; upon the willow branches, the spring of the second month. Having lost his eyes, he has picked them up.
Bi: Having followed the teachings, I fell into the dust and wind;

dwelling in knowledge, I returned to my home in Wu, to the misty waters and marshlands of the Wusong. The distant ancient road reaches as far as heaven; when we meet, what need is there to discuss guest and host?
Master! A single phrase is clear and leaves nothing hidden;

though the ocean of mystery has a thousand layers and a hundred folds that do not let a breeze through, who can exhaust its source and reach the emptiness of kalpas? If you understand it, even a single bubble has never existed.
Setting forth: The surging Yangtze and Han rivers all flow toward the capital.
Sending off Chan Master Zhi, the *vyanināyaka*, as he travels to Jinling;
Kebin does not enter the monastic community. Xinghua vainly employs the "trap for tigers" device. Tomorrow, by the side of Stonehead City.
Departing, I, an old man in the empty mountains, gaze toward my eastern return.
Master Cun has paid homage at Mount Emei, Mount Wutai, and traveled to Mount Tiantai;
now returning to Jiangxi, he remains within the golden realm amidst the silver realm. Not a single step of his feet has ever moved. If Hanshan were to see him at Mount Tiantai...
My son, you should ask the horse-winnowing basket of Jiangxi.
If Bodhidharma never came to the Eastern Land and the Second Patriarch never went to the Western Heaven, then when you realize that the flowers bloom in five petals, cease your talk.
A separate transmission outside the teachings.
The great Japanese Tripitaka Master, the Reverend Shō, who clarified the Way in the land of Tang;
the National Teacher of Fusang. The unperforated flute of Shaolin—let it blow freely against the wind.
Moving through the mountains in the four modes of deportment, my staff of seven feet is held aloft. Turning my head toward the pine-gated pass, the setting sun already lingers over the village ahead.
Dwelling within these mountains, do not expose the family’s hidden flaws. Coarse rice with plain yellow pickles—no salt and no vinegar.
Sitting in the mountains: good causes invite evil fruits. Old Dharma, you bald barbarian, you have needlessly become a laughingstock.
Lying in the mountains: a rat passes by the head of the bed; looking up at the roof beam, one realizes not a single person truly knows the mind.
The Song of the Twelve Hours:
The Cock Crows at the Hour of Chou (1–3 a.m.). Having grasped the nostrils, one loses the mouth. At every gate and threshold, there is a clamor;
Li Si and Zhang San vie with one another to run forward.
At dawn, at the hour of Yin (5–7 a.m.): In the world, one should rely on the provisional rather than the real. One must carve out one’s own belly; there is no need to lower one’s head and ask others.

At sunrise, at the hour of Mao (7–9 a.m.): Plucking grass and picking flowers, they compete for cleverness. Do not let them run into a true practitioner, lest they be left in a state of utter disorder.
This occasion is no small matter.
At the hour of eating, one might boil five *he* of yellow millet in a sand pot; though coarse food may easily satisfy the hunger, its flavor is truly genuine only when chewed slowly.
At the hour of *yuzhong* (Yi): From birth to old age, it is exactly like this. Bodhidharma needlessly thrusts his head out, only to have his front teeth knocked out by others.
At the hour of *rinan* (Wu): Suffering within joy, joy within suffering; the Unranked True Person laughs until his cheeks are exposed. The lantern swallows—
Yet the bright pillar is revealed.
Before the sun has turned its course, who can recognize you with your demonic faces and divine heads? If you ask "how" at this critical moment, I shall cast them all at once into the Long River.
The hour of *shen* (the seventh watch). The view from the window is vast and empty, with not a neighbor in sight. Do not be surprised that there is no tea for guests;
a single cup of mugwort broth shall suffice as my sincere hospitality.
The hour of *you* (the eighth watch). There remains but one pair of hands, those of a destitute man. At the mere snap of a finger, the gates of the pavilion open, and the youth Sudhana enters.
The Son meets his first friend at dusk, during the hour of Xu (7–9 p.m.). Lacking density in his own practice, he gathers his robes and sits alone in deep reflection:
"Today it is six, and tomorrow it will be seven."
At the hour of Ren-ding (Hai), one must simply remain ever-awake. In shallow grass and level fields, divergent paths abound;
do not let your feet slip into the ocean of ignorance.
At the hour of Zhong-yè (Zi), falling down by oneself, one naturally rises again. Seeking once more after the remnants of a dream, no trace remains; before one realizes it, day has broken.
The Paper-Window of Clarity. *The Recorded Sayings of Master Pingshi* (End).
When Master Pingshi of Tiantong first met the old Yuan Ying at Lufeng, it was like ascending Mount Dongshan and seeing the state of Lu as small. He then visited Linglongyan again. Like...
"Having ascended Mount Tai, one sees the world as small. Thirty years later, he followed in the footsteps of his ancestors' old ways, expanding the influence of his family lineage.
He manipulated power, exercising control over bestowal and withdrawal, acting with such defiance that he was like a starving wildcat glaring back at its father.
He smashed the sand pot to pieces, extinguished the gentle embers of the fire, snapped the reeds and weeds like arrows, and tore through the iron mesh. This was the Way of the Master.

At this point, his radiance became magnificent and vast, like the solitary moon among the myriad stars. As former masters have said: "If Yangqi had not received Baiyun, he would not have attained Bao Ning;
if Huidang had not received Siling, he would not have attained Yuan. Others who were merely mediocre and commonplace could hardly be considered worthy of following in their footsteps.
